svg.text: Browning does not create red absorption — it MOVES it
the same total, split differently between the two bands
the same thing, in the numbers a metric uses
Q% reads ONE end of this see-saw. A DIFFERENCE reads the
whole tilt — and drops the pivot entirely.
Q% = pivot + ½·tilt 624 end = pivot − ½·tilt
the same pivot, plus and minus the SAME half-tilt
the SAME grey pivot sits under all four band bars — it is TOTAL PIGMENT, not roast, and it wobbles on every refill
⇒ a metric built as a DIFFERENCE collects both gaps AND discards the pivot, which is ~90 % of Q%'s number and none of its signal
Class means over the 88 labelled isopropanol runs of the report archive (55 green / 33 brown; diffuser-IN runs and the opaque fill excluded). Every bar is
100 × [ A(band) − A(500–560) ] / A(448–460), so it is concentration-free and the Soret is the ruler — which is why the blue bar reads 100.
⚠ The roast weakens the Soret too, so the ruler is not perfectly fixed; we read its FLANK (448–460 nm), not its peak (~432 nm).
⚠ The “tilt” drawn here is NOT the shipped dQ100, which divides by sd(448–626) instead: green 3.8, brown 44.1. The two track each other at r = 0.992, so the
mechanism transfers — the scale does not. Q%, by contrast, is drawn here exactly.
